findings.highlight: I’ll load the plates and you can take them out.
findings.evidenceJa: お皿にはわたしが盛りますから、先輩はお茶碗を出してください
findings.governingReading: Sakura proposes a division of serving: she will portion the food onto plates while Shirou takes out the rice bowls.
findings.explanation: Load the plates is nonidiomatic for serving food, while take them out makes plates the apparent object and removes the separate rice bowls Shirou is assigned to fetch.

findings.highlight: …I think we intended to do it until my injury healed, but some trivial thing came up to make her stay with it.
findings.evidenceJa: ……俺のケガが治るまで、と決めていたように思えるのだが、なにかほんっとーに些細な出来事があって、なんとなーく家事手伝いを続けてもらう事になったような。
findings.governingReading: Shirou twice marks the memory as uncertain: he seems to recall setting his recovery as the endpoint, then vaguely recalls some truly trivial event after which Sakura somehow continued helping with the housework.
findings.explanation: The English keeps the first hedge but turns the second half into a definite causal event that made Sakura continue, removing the narrator's stretched, evasive uncertainty and changing an arrangement into pressure on her agency.
